results.title: Develop Risk Mitigation Plans
results.content: Risks are monitored and when they exceed the established thresholds, the risk mitigation plans are deployed to return the impacted effort to an acceptable risk level. If the risk cannot be mitigated, a contingency plan may be invoked. Both risk mitigation and contingency plans are often generated only for selected risks where the consequences of the risks are determined to be high or unacceptable; other risks may be accepted and simply monitored. _Risks are watched when there is an objectively defined, verifiable, and documented threshold of performance, time, or risk exposure (the combination of likelihood and consequence) that will trigger risk mitigation planning or invoke a contingency plan if it is needed_. Adequate consideration should be given early to technology demonstrations, models, simulations, and prototypes as part of risk mitigation planning prioritization are sometimes called “risk assessment” or “risk analysis.” * Determine the levels and thresholds that define when a risk becomes unacceptable and triggers the execution of a risk mitigation plan or a contingency plan. Typically, thresholds for the execution of risk mitigation plans are set to engage before the execution of contingency plans. * Determine the cost-to-benefit ratio of implementing the risk mitigation plan for each risk. * Develop an overall risk mitigation plan for the project to orchestrate the implementation of the individual risk mitigation and contingency plans. The complete set of risk mitigation plans may not be affordable. A tradeoff analysis should be performed to prioritize the risk mitigation plans for implementation. * Develop contingency plans for selected critical risks in the event their impacts are realized. Risk mitigation plans are developed and implemented as needed to proactively reduce risks before they become problems. Contingency plans can be developed for critical risks to describe the actions a project may take to deal with the occurrence of this impact. The intent is to define a proactive plan for handling the risk, either to reduce the risk (mitigation) or respond to the risk (contingency), but in either event to manage the risk. Some risk management literature may consider contingency plans a synonym or subset of risk mitigation plans.

results.title: [PDF] 7. Trigger Finger - Clinical Threshold Referral Criteria - BEST
results.content: The symptoms can include: - Pain/ Stiffness/ Clicking/ and a small lump (nodule) of tissue at the base of the affected finger or thumb A Cochrane review has found evidence supporting initial treatment using single corticosteroid injections, before considering referral for surgery. As corticosteroid injection is an easy, less invasive, inexpensive treatment modality, therefore NHS England feel that the initial treatment for Trigger Finger patients should be corticosteroid injection rather than surgery. Criteria for Commissioning- Barnsley CCG will only fund surgery for patients diagnosed with Trigger Finger in the following circumstances: Yes No Failure to respond to Conservative/ non-invasive treatment method eg Exercise/massage Rest from aggravating activity Splinting NSAIDS AND Failure to respond to At least one corticosteroid injection (Rotherham guideline-max 2 injections with a 10 week interval between injections) OR Fixed flexion deformity That cannot be corrected by conservative measures OR Where corticosteroid injection is contraindicated Patient Name: Address: Date of Birth: NHS Number Consultant/Service to whom referral will be made: Please send this form with the referral letter.

# [Why is a common LED failure mode to flicker astably or oscillate? [closed]](/questions/290171/why-is-a-common-led-failure-mode-to-flicker-astably-or-oscillate). Will someone "in the know" please cast some light (so to speak) on the apparently common shortcoming in the electronic design of commercial LED driver circuits which is the root cause of this ubiquitous problem? LED's pretty much do what the voltage you feed into them does, if you see an LED flickering it is most likely due to its voltage source. The forward voltage is not just current dependent but temperature and varies with the fabrication process from one LED to the next even coming off the manufacturing line one after another. When LEDs are strung in series the forward voltages vary unpredictably. > You also say, "When LEDs are strung in series the forward voltages vary unpredictably." I think you may be confusing series with parallel. This flicker is in the 100-200 Hz range from poorly designed and PWM dimming LED drivers. The following is an article about flicker, saccadic eye movement, and poor LED designs at the cause. How to design an LED circuit to not have flicker. Designing to Mitigate the Effects of Flicker in LED Lighting. Example this article Buck Regulators Make Driving High Brightness LEDs Easy  says "You can overvoltage the switch, you can overvoltage the current-sense pin, and basically have anything from a little bit of LED flicker to a destroyed device.". I see lots of very bad LED designs and I do see low frequency flicker in the Lab. results.content: Analysis of Flicker Phenomenon in LED Lighting and Mitigation Solutions. # Analysis of Flicker Phenomenon in LED Lighting and Mitigation Solutions. 1 What is Flicker in LED Lighting? 3 Causes of Flicker in LED Lighting. 6 Mitigation Solutions for Flicker in LED Lighting. However, an often-overlooked issue in LED lighting systems is the flicker phenomenon. This article provides an in-depth analysis of flicker in LED lighting, its causes, effects, measurement methods, and effective mitigation solutions, empowering you to select high-quality LED lighting for residential and professional environments. # What is Flicker in LED Lighting? * Flicker in both high-end LED lighting and lower-quality products can lead to issues such as:. * Understanding and mitigating flicker in LED lighting is critical to ensuring high-quality illumination systems and protecting user well-being. # Causes of Flicker in LED Lighting. The flicker phenomenon in LED lighting systems not only degrades light quality but also has significant adverse effects:. * In environments requiring high precision, such as industrial LED lighting or film studios, flicker can degrade image quality or cause distractions. Flicker diminishes the visual experience, particularly in applications like smart LED lighting or decorative LED lighting, affecting user comfort and reducing the perceived value of the lighting product. * ENERGY STAR: Requires energy-efficient LED lighting to meet flicker standards for quality assurance. * IEC 61000-4-15: Defines flicker measurement standards for electrical systems, applicable to both industrial LED lighting and residential products. # Mitigation Solutions for Flicker in LED Lighting. To minimize flicker and enhance the performance of LED lighting systems, consider the following solutions:. * Direct Current (DC) Power: DC eliminates AC-induced oscillations, reducing flicker in high-power LED lighting. * Flicker-Free Technology: Leading manufacturers like Philips and Osram offer high-end LED lighting with flicker mitigation technology for stable output. * Specialized Lighting: LED studio lighting and LED stage lighting demand flicker-free performance for high-quality visuals. * Advanced LED Drivers: Manufacturers are developing cost-effective, high-performance drivers to minimize flicker in energy-efficient LED lighting. The flicker phenomenon in LED lighting is a critical issue that affects light quality and user health.
